source.title: Training Aware Sigmoidal Optimizer
source.authors: David Macêdo; Pedro Dreyer; Teresa B Ludermir; C. Zanchettin

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper, though the conclusion and some section transitions are affected by PDF extraction artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on image-classification test accuracy using a different schedule and optimizer set than the claim's cited comparisons; it does not measure the training–test gap directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy for adaptive optimizers, SGD variants, and TASO. Rows concern V4's optimizer-performance comparison. Its results do not measure train–test gaps, random-label memorization, width, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Cited claims about adaptive optimizers in the Introduction are not treated as results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses the adaptive-optimizer generalization finding to motivate TASO and evaluates its proposed method against adaptive optimizers. TASO is a nonadaptive SGD learning-rate schedule, used here with momentum, but these comparisons report the proposed method's performance. The remaining SGD results are hyperparameter-selection results, not an independent final comparison testing V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' overall conclusion: they claim TASO outperforms adaptive optimizers and interpret this as possible evidence of overfitting. Qualify that claim with their explicit MNIST equivalence finding. Their overfitting interpretation is not established by the reported final test metrics. The text's claimed ResNet18 advantage exceeding two percentage points also conflicts with Table IX, which shows 0.80 percentage points over AMSGrad.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares an automated sigmoidal learning-rate schedule with adaptive optimizers, and includes an SGD learning-rate search; it does not reproduce the cited adaptive-versus-SGD study's benchmark set or full comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with optimizer, learning rate, model, dataset, and training duration; the paper reports 100-epoch and 25-epoch results for VGG19 on CIFAR10.

fits_no_version.finding: TASO outperformed AMSGrad on CIFAR tasks: 91.98 versus 91.33 on VGG19/CIFAR10 at 100 epochs, 90.02 versus 88.56 at 25 epochs, 65.08 versus 61.46 on VGG19/CIFAR100, and 93.15 versus 92.35 on ResNet18/CIFAR10. On LeNet5/MNIST, TASO and RMSProp both reached 99.09, versus AMSGrad's 99.03; the authors considered these methods equivalent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed TASO schedule improves held-out accuracy over the tested adaptive optimizers in these CIFAR experiments, with near-equivalent performance among TASO, RMSProp, and AMSGrad on MNIST.

record.problems: The paper reports test accuracy and loss, but the final optimizer comparisons do not include SGD. SGD appears only in the constant-learning-rate search, so the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison required by V4 is not matched across the reported final-result conditions. The study does not report training accuracy in those final comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. For V4, the SGD search includes many learning rates and momentum variants in Table IV; only the 0.05 entries are retained as representative SGD comparator results. Other learning-rate entries do not resolve the lack of a matched final comparison.

untested.parts: Generalization as width increases beyond interpolation.

An independent adaptive-versus-SGD comparison beyond the proposed-method evaluation; language benchmarks; matched training performance; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.

record.verdict_notes: TASO is itself scheduled SGD with momentum in these experiments; saying the study contains no SGD-based final comparator would be misleading. Its exclusion here rests on the proposed-method evaluation rule. All reported accuracy uncertainties are standard deviations across five runs.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels are not tested.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No language benchmarks; no explicit training-accuracy comparison for the final optimizer results; no decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure analysis.
